sun-hail.context: A sun peeking out from behind a cloud with round hailstones falling below. Used in weather forecasts and apps for hail showers with sunny spells during the day.

moon-hail.context: A crescent moon behind a cloud with round hailstones falling below. Marks hail showers at night in forecasts and weather apps.

sun-sleet.context: A sun behind a cloud with a raindrop and a snowflake falling together. Shows sleet or a wintry mix of rain and snow with sunny spells in a forecast.

moon-sleet.context: A crescent moon behind a cloud with a raindrop and a snowflake falling. Marks sleet or a mix of rain and snow at night in weather forecasts.

isolated-thunderstorm.context: A sun behind a cloud with a single lightning bolt below it. Used in forecasts for isolated or scattered thunderstorms on an otherwise sunny day.

severe-thunderstorm.context: A heavy storm cloud with a lightning bolt and hailstones falling beside it. Used for severe thunderstorm watches, warnings and dangerous storm alerts.

hazy-sun.context: A sun partly covered by horizontal haze lines across its lower half. Used in weather apps for hazy sunshine, dust haze, smoke haze and poor visibility.

moon-fog.context: A crescent moon above bands of fog. Marks fog or mist at night in forecasts, weather apps and road safety notices.

moon-wind.context: A crescent moon with curling gusts of wind below. Shows windy or breezy conditions at night in weather apps and forecasts.

cloud-ceiling.context: A cloud with a double headed arrow reaching down to the ground line. Shows cloud ceiling or cloud base height in aviation weather reports and forecasts.

relative-humidity.context: A water drop with a percent sign inside it. Shows relative humidity readings on weather apps, thermostats, hygrometers and indoor climate displays.

tropical-night.context: A crescent moon beside a thermometer reading high. Marks a tropical night or a warm night when temperatures stay high after dark.

degree-days.context: A thermometer standing beside a calendar page. Used for heating and cooling degree days in energy reports, building management and agriculture.

outdoor-temperature.context: A thermometer standing outside beside a house. Shows the outside temperature on smart home apps, thermostats and weather stations.

cloud-in-a-jar.context: A glass jar with a lid and a small cloud floating inside. Used for the classroom cloud in a jar experiment and science lessons on condensation.

cut-off-low.context: A wavy jet stream line above a detached closed circle holding the letter L. Marks a cut off low pressure system on weather maps and in forecast discussions.

albedo.context: Sunlight striking a white ice sheet and bouncing back up as a reflected arrow. Explains albedo, surface reflectivity and the ice albedo feedback in climate science.

climate-tipping-point.context: A ball balanced on the crest of a hill beside a small thermometer. Stands for climate tipping points and thresholds beyond which change becomes self reinforcing.

solar-radiation.context: A sun in the corner sending parallel arrows down onto the ground. Shows solar radiation, insolation and sunlight intensity in weather and energy apps.

freezing-level.context: A mountain with a dashed freezing line across its middle and a snowflake above. Marks the freezing level or snow line height in mountain and aviation forecasts.

temperature-inversion.context: A valley with smoke trapped and spreading under a flat warm lid of air. Explains temperature inversions that hold smog and pollution close to the ground.

growing-season.context: A calendar page with a seedling sprouting inside. Marks the growing season, frost free period and planting calendar for gardens and farms.

plant-hardiness-zone.context: A potted plant beside a map divided into banded zones. Used for plant hardiness zones and climate zones in gardening guides and nurseries.

soil-moisture.context: A block of soil with a water drop inside under a gauge needle. Shows soil moisture readings from sensors used in irrigation, farming and drought monitoring.

evapotranspiration.context: A plant on the ground with wavy vapour arrows rising from the soil on both sides. Explains evapotranspiration and water loss in irrigation planning and hydrology.

surface-runoff.context: Rain falling on a sloped ground with an arrow showing water running down the slope. Explains surface runoff, stormwater and flash flooding in hydrology.

wind-erosion.context: A plowed field with soil blowing off it along a curling wind line. Shows wind erosion, dust storms and soil loss on dry farmland.

wet-bulb-thermometer.context: A thermometer whose bulb is wrapped in a wick dipping into a cup of water. Used for wet bulb temperature, psychrometers and heat stress readings.

evaporation-pan.context: A wide shallow round pan on a low stand with a measuring rod above it. Stands for evaporation pans used at weather stations to measure water loss.

dropsonde.context: A small instrument tube hanging below a parachute. Stands for dropsondes released from aircraft to measure temperature, humidity and wind inside storms.

argo-float.context: A tall slim float bobbing upright in the waves with an antenna on top. Stands for ocean profiling floats that measure sea temperature and salinity.

flux-tower.context: A tall lattice tower rising above the treetops with instruments on an arm at the top. Stands for flux towers that measure carbon dioxide, water and energy exchange.

weather-station-display.context: A small tabletop screen showing a sun symbol and a temperature readout. Used for home weather stations, indoor and outdoor displays and forecast gadgets.

hurricane-hunter-aircraft.context: A propeller aircraft flying toward a hurricane spiral. Stands for hurricane hunter and storm reconnaissance flights that collect data inside tropical cyclones.

weather-ship.context: A ship with a radar dome on its cabin and a weather balloon rising from the deck. Stands for weather ships and ocean research vessels that observe marine weather.

hail-net.context: A fruit tree under a net stretched between poles with hailstones bouncing off above. Used for anti hail netting that protects orchards and crops.

hail-cannon.context: An upright cone shaped cannon pointing at the sky with sound rings rising from its mouth. Stands for hail cannons used on farms and vineyards to try to prevent hail.

polar-research-station.context: A boxy research station raised on stilts above the snow with an antenna mast beside it. Stands for Antarctic and Arctic bases and polar science.

weather-wheel.context: A round chart split into weather segments with a pointer in the centre. Used in classrooms and for kids to show today's weather.

cloud-watching.context: A person lying on their back in the grass looking up at a cloud. Used for cloud watching, daydreaming, relaxing outdoors and mindfulness.

storm-chasing.context: A van with a roof instrument rack driving toward a tornado. Stands for storm chasing, storm spotters and severe weather field research.

rain-ripple.context: Raindrops falling onto water with a ripple ring spreading outward. Used for rain on water, puddles, rain sounds and calm rainy moods.

scud-cloud.context: A low cloud base with ragged torn wisps of cloud hanging below it. Used for scud or fractus clouds in cloud identification and storm spotting.

black-globe-thermometer.context: A black globe on a short stand with a thermometer through its top. Used for globe temperature and wet bulb globe temperature heat stress measurements.

thermoscope.context: A glass bulb on top of a long thin tube dipped upside down into a flask of water. Shows the early air thermoscope from the history of science.

propeller-anemometer.context: A streamlined wind sensor with a propeller in front and a tail fin on a pole. Measures wind speed and direction at weather stations and wind farms.

pyrheliometer.context: A long narrow tube on a tracking mount pointed straight at the sun. Measures direct sunlight for solar energy and radiation research.

weather-logbook.context: A notebook with a small sun at the top and ruled columns of entries below. Used for weather diaries, observation logs and daily weather records.

penitentes.context: Tall narrow pointed snow blades leaning toward a small sun. Shows penitentes, the ice spikes that form on high mountain glaciers in strong sunlight.

frost-heave.context: A road surface pushed up into a bulge above an ice lens in the soil. Shows frost heave, freeze thaw road damage and frozen ground.

headwind.context: A cyclist leaning forward into wind lines blowing straight at them. Used for headwinds in cycling, running and travel apps, and wind resistance.

wind-load.context: A tall building with arrows of wind pushing against one side. Used for wind load and wind pressure in structural engineering and building design.

volcanic-winter.context: A volcano under a wide ash veil with a snowflake below. Stands for volcanic winter, the cooling that follows large eruptions that fill the sky with ash.

carbon-budget.context: A measuring cylinder with a cloud of carbon inside and a dashed limit line near the top. Stands for the remaining carbon budget and emissions limits.

wave-height.context: An ocean wave with a double headed arrow from trough to crest. Shows wave height, swell size and sea state in marine and surf forecasts.

melting-snowman.context: A snowman slumped into a puddle with its hat tilted and the sun above it. Used for thaw, warm winters, melting snow and climate change messages.

snow-covered-car.context: A car with a thick rounded layer of snow piled on its roof. Used for snowed in cars, winter driving advice and clearing snow.

weather-drone.context: A quadcopter drone carrying a sensor pod below a cloud. Stands for weather drones that profile the atmosphere and collect meteorological data.

volcanic-lightning.context: A volcano with a tall ash plume lit by two lightning bolts. Shows volcanic lightning, also called a dirty thunderstorm, during eruptions.

hodograph.context: A circular polar grid with a curving line of dots running out from the centre. Used for hodographs that show wind shear with height in storm forecasting.

castellanus-cloud.context: A flat cloud layer with a row of turret towers rising from its top. Used for castellanus clouds, a sign of unstable air and later thunderstorms.

horseshoe-cloud.context: A small arched cloud shaped like an upside down U. Shows the rare horseshoe vortex cloud in cloud identification and sky photography.

burning-earth.context: A globe with flames rising from its top edge. Used for global warming, the climate crisis and messages about a planet overheating.

earth-hourglass.context: An hourglass with a small globe in the top bulb and sand gathered in the bottom. Stands for time running out for the planet and climate deadlines.

avalanche-danger-scale.context: A snowy mountain beside five rising bars like a hazard rating. Shows the avalanche danger level in mountain and backcountry forecasts.

capped-column-snowflake.context: A short ice column capped by a wide flat hexagonal plate at each end, like a spool. Shows the capped column snow crystal type.

grass-minimum-thermometer.context: A thermometer lying on two forked stands just above the grass. Measures the grass minimum temperature and ground frost at weather stations.

intertropical-convergence-zone.context: A globe with a band of clouds along the equator and arrows meeting it from north and south. Explains the intertropical convergence zone and the trade winds.

front-cross-section.context: A side view of a wedge of cold air pushing under warm air that rises into a cloud. Explains weather fronts and frontal lifting in meteorology lessons.
